s: Clover Health DEF 14A filed 28 Apr 2026 (ownership as of 31 Mar 2026); CLOV close 4.14 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 92,175,636 Class B plus 1,409,267 Class A = 93,584,903 shares x 4.14 = 387M; excludes 12.7M unvested performance RSUs
did: Bought three failing Hudson County hospitals out of bankruptcy from 2008 (Bayonne, Christ, Hoboken University Medical Center) and ran them out-of-network, then used the cash to found Clover Health in 2014, a Medicare Advantage plan built around its own Clover Assistant software. Took it public via SPAC in January 2021.
why: Medicare Advantage pays a risk-adjusted capitated rate per member, so margin comes from documenting disease burden accurately, not from narrowing the network. Clover bet a cheap physician-facing software layer could do that inside a wide-open PPO, which let it sell the one product seniors actually want.
obst: Hindenburg Research published in February 2021, days after the SPAC closed, revealing an undisclosed DOJ civil investigative demand tied to his hospital billing; the stock fell roughly 80 percent, securities suits followed, and his CarePoint hospital group filed Chapter 11 in 2024.
turn: The 2023 decision to shut the loss-making ACO REACH business and run only the insurance plan, which took Clover to its first profitable year in 2025 and re-rated the stock.

s: Johnson & Johnson DEF 14A filed 11 Mar 2026 (ownership as of 24 Feb 2026); JNJ close 270.24 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 356,297 shares = 96M, plus 1,256,655 options with 151M intrinsic at 270.24, plus 31.7M pension present value and 10.2M deferred comp; excludes unearned PSUs at maximum
did: Joined J&J in Spain in 1989 as a sales trainee, ran the worldwide pharmaceutical group from 2011, and became chairman and CEO in January 2022. In May 2023 he spun the consumer-health business out as Kenvue, turning J&J into a pure pharmaceutical and medtech company for the first time in 137 years.
why: J&J grants deep-in-the-money option tranches every February with three-year cliffs and never repriced them. Thirty-seven years of that, against a share price that went from 156 to 270 between 2025 and 2026 on Darzalex, Tremfya and Carvykti, converts a salaried career into a nine-figure option position.
obst: Talc liability: three separate attempts to push the claims into a Texas two-step bankruptcy were rejected by federal courts, the last in March 2025, forcing him to litigate roughly 60,000 ovarian-cancer claims in the ordinary tort system while running the company.
turn: The May 2023 Kenvue IPO, which raised 3.8 billion dollars, removed the low-growth consumer segment and let J&J be valued on its oncology and immunology pipeline.

s: Insmed DEF 14A filed 1 Apr 2026 (ownership as of record date; option table as of 31 Dec 2025); INSM close 125.77 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 382,484 shares = 48M, plus 2,036,065 options with 203M intrinsic at 125.77, plus 166,777 unvested units = 21M; total 272M pre-tax
did: Took over Insmed in September 2012 when it was a roughly 150 million dollar shell left from a reverse merger, and spent thirteen years pushing two programs through the FDA. Brinsupri, the first drug ever approved for bronchiectasis, cleared in August 2025 and carried the company past 27 billion dollars.
why: Bronchiectasis had no approved therapy anywhere in the world, so a positive phase 3 created a monopoly rather than a share fight. Lewis kept the DPP-1 mechanism in-house instead of partnering it away, and paid himself almost entirely in ten-year options struck between 13 and 34 dollars.
obst: The 2016 European phase 2 of ARIKAYCE in refractory NTM missed its primary endpoint and the shares lost more than half their value; the FDA later put Insmed through an advisory committee before granting accelerated approval in 2018 on a surrogate sputum-conversion endpoint.
turn: The ASPEN phase 3 readout for brensocatib in May 2024, which hit on exacerbation reduction and roughly doubled the stock in a single session.

s: Innodata DEF 14A filed 24 Apr 2026; Form 4 of 16 Jun 2026; Forms 4 aggregated 2023-2026; INOD close 64.81 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 1,340,456 shares = 87M plus roughly 746,000 options struck 1.24-7.24 worth about 47M, plus 162M of gross Form 4 sale proceeds since 2023 taken after tax at roughly 60 percent
did: Became CEO of Innodata in 1997, when it was a small offshore data-conversion shop serving publishers, and spent two decades running a sub-2-dollar microcap. From 2018 he redeployed that offshore workforce into machine-learning training data, and by 2024 the big US model labs were his largest customers.
why: Frontier labs needed tens of thousands of trained, managed, security-cleared annotators on short notice. Innodata already had that workforce and twenty-five years of delivery process built for publishers, so it could sign enterprise-grade contracts that venture-funded labelling startups could not staff.
obst: Innodata traded below 2 dollars for most of the 2010s as its legacy publishing-services revenue shrank; he financed the AI pivot out of operating cash with no outside capital, and a short-seller report in February 2024 accused the company of overstating its AI business.
turn: The 2023 contract expansion with a single large technology customer, which took revenue from 79 million to 171 million dollars in one year and re-rated the stock from about 2 dollars to above 40.

s: Johnson & Johnson DEF 14A filed 11 Mar 2026 and Form 10-K filed 11 Feb 2026 (age); JNJ close 270.24 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 194,451 shares = 52M, plus 639,402 options with 76M intrinsic at 270.24, plus 37,441 earned units = 10M, plus 17.8M deferred comp and 11.0M pension
did: Joined J&J in 2005 as a worldwide vice president and has run Innovative Medicine, its 60 billion dollar drug business, since 2018. She built the multiple-myeloma franchise around Darzalex and the CAR-T therapy Carvykti and pushed the 30 billion dollar Actelion purchase into a pulmonary-hypertension leadership position.
why: Running the segment that carries J&J's option grants meant her pay was almost all ten-year options and performance shares struck between 115 and 166 dollars. Darzalex passing 12 billion dollars of annual sales while she held the tranches is what turned executive compensation into a nine-figure holding.
obst: Stelara, her largest single product at roughly 10 billion dollars a year, lost US exclusivity to biosimilars starting in 2025; she had to replace that revenue inside the same segment while the talc litigation consumed board attention.
turn: Her 2018 appointment to run Worldwide Pharmaceuticals, which put her in charge of the Actelion integration and the oncology portfolio at the moment Darzalex moved into frontline therapy.

s: Merck DEF 14A filed 8 Apr 2026 (ownership as of 28 Feb 2026); MRK close 152.55 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 443,602 shares = 68M, plus 1,074,291 options with 61M intrinsic at 152.55, plus 204,357 earned and vesting units = 31M; excludes unearned PSUs at maximum
did: Joined Merck as chief financial officer in 2014 from Baxter and became chief executive in January 2021. He has spent his tenure buying his way out of the 2028 Keytruda patent cliff, including the 10.8 billion dollar Prometheus deal in 2023 and the 10 billion dollar Verona Pharma purchase in 2025.
why: Merck grants ten-year options every May at the closing price. Davis accumulated tranches struck between 73 and 87 dollars during the 2019-2022 stretch when the market discounted Keytruda's durability; the shares later trading at 152 turned those grants into most of his balance sheet.
obst: Keytruda, roughly 45 percent of Merck's revenue, loses US exclusivity in 2028, and the Gardasil business collapsed in China in 2024-2025; he had to fund replacement pipeline while the stock fell from 130 to under 80.
turn: The 2021 spin-off of Organon, which stripped out the mature women's-health and legacy-brand portfolio and forced Merck to be valued on oncology alone.

s: Insmed DEF 14A filed 1 Apr 2026 (option table as of 31 Dec 2025); INSM close 125.77 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 1,418,400 options struck 13.67-67.22 with 146M intrinsic at 125.77, plus 47,389 shares = 6M and 67,875 unvested units = 8.5M
did: Joined Insmed in September 2016 as chief commercial officer and became chief operating officer, building the launch organisation for ARIKAYCE in refractory non-tuberculous mycobacterial lung disease and then for Brinsupri, the first approved bronchiectasis drug, in 2025.
why: He joined a company whose shares were under 15 dollars and took his compensation in ten-year options; Insmed granted him roughly 1.4 million of them at strikes between 13.67 and 34 dollars before the 2024 brensocatib readout. Almost all of his net worth is the spread on those grants.
obst: ARIKAYCE launched in 2018 into a disease with no diagnostic infrastructure and no treating-physician habit; he had to build the identification pathway for NTM patients from scratch while the drug carried a boxed warning for respiratory adverse reactions.
turn: The August 2025 US approval of Brinsupri, which gave him a primary-care-scale bronchiectasis launch rather than a rare-disease one.

s: Burlington Stores DEF 14A filed 2 Apr 2026 (ownership as of 1 Dec 2025); BURL close 326.50 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 170,439 shares = 56M, plus 350,275 options with 45M intrinsic at 326.50, plus 54,768 earned PSUs and 37,456 RSUs = 30M
did: Left Ross Stores in 2019 after fifteen years as its chief operating officer to run Burlington, and rebuilt it around a 25,000 square-foot prototype store, faster inventory turns and opportunistic in-season buying. Store count and comparable sales grew and the shares tripled from the 2020 low.
why: Off-price retail earns on inventory turns, not markup. Cutting the box in half doubled the number of viable sites, and buying closer to the season let Burlington carry less inventory per store, which is exactly the model Ross runs and Burlington had never fully adopted.
obst: He had been CEO for six months when COVID closed every store in March 2020; Burlington had no e-commerce to fall back on, shut its website entirely, and had to raise emergency convertible notes and secured debt in April 2020 to survive.
turn: The 2020-2021 decision to shrink the prototype store to about 25,000 square feet and reset the buying organisation, which cut new-store capital cost and lifted sales per foot.

s: Johnson & Johnson DEF 14A filed 11 Mar 2026 and Form 10-K filed 11 Feb 2026 (age); JNJ close 270.24 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 85,008 shares = 23M, plus 620,976 options with 72M intrinsic at 270.24, plus 148,603 units = 40M, plus 13.5M pension and 1.9M deferred comp
did: Joined J&J in 1998 and became chief financial officer in 2018. He financed and executed the 2023 Kenvue separation, the largest consumer-health carve-out ever attempted, and the 14.6 billion dollar Intra-Cellular Therapies purchase in 2025.
why: The CFO seat at J&J carries the second-largest option grant in the company, issued annually at the closing price with a three-year cliff. Twenty-eight years of grants, most struck between 115 and 166 dollars, against a 270 dollar share price is where essentially all of the value sits.
obst: He had to fund the Kenvue split without an investment-grade downgrade while J&J was carrying an unquantified talc liability that had already been rejected twice by the bankruptcy courts, and while the debt markets repriced through 2022.
turn: The 2023 Kenvue split-off exchange offer, which retired roughly 190 million J&J shares and let the parent redeploy the proceeds into pharmaceutical acquisitions.

s: CompoSecure Form 4 of 17 Sep 2024 and 13 May 2024; CompoSecure DEF 14A filed 18 Apr 2024 (age 57); GPGI close 12.79 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 16,596,214 shares sold at 7.55 plus 2,968,065 at 6.50 = 145M gross, taken after tax at roughly 66 percent, plus 2,043,320 retained shares at 12.79
did: Started as a programmer analyst at Prudential, then co-founded CompoSecure in Somerset, New Jersey in 2002 to manufacture metal payment cards. She was general manager to 2012, chief executive to 2017 and executive chairman to 2021, took the company public via SPAC in December 2021 and sold most of her stake in 2024.
why: A metal card costs an issuer roughly twenty times a plastic one and cannot be produced on standard card lines, so the whole category is a manufacturing bottleneck. CompoSecure owned the US capacity and the security certifications, which meant every premium card programme had to come to it.
obst: She was a woman running a card-manufacturing plant in an industry controlled by three European conglomerates, and had to persuade issuers that a heavy card was a retention tool rather than a novelty; the SPAC listing then left the stock trading under 6 dollars for two years.
turn: The 2016 launch of the JPMorgan Chase Sapphire Reserve on a CompoSecure metal blank, which made the metal card a mass-market status object and pulled every other issuer into the category.

s: Bel Fuse DEF 14A filed 10 Apr 2026 (age 72; ownership as of record date); BELFB close 255.46 on 21 Aug 2026
m: 381,975 Class A and 27,777 Class B beneficially owned, valued at about 240 per share, plus 63,557 Class A and 42,965 Class B in trusts of which he is a beneficiary
did: Son of Bel Fuse's founder, he joined the Jersey City fuse maker in the late 1970s, became president in 1992 and chief executive in 2001, and ran it until May 2025. He turned a single-product fuse company into a power-conversion and connectivity supplier through roughly twenty acquisitions.
why: Bel bought orphaned magnetics, connector and power lines that larger firms were exiting, kept the qualified part numbers and the design-in positions, and never had to win a socket twice. When AI racks moved to high-density 48-volt power, those legacy qualifications became the scarce asset.
obst: The 2014 purchase of Emerson's Power Solutions business for about 98 million dollars loaded the balance sheet with debt just as the acquired business missed plan; the shares fell from the high twenties to the mid teens and stayed there for most of the following five years.
turn: The 2024 acquisition of Enercon, which added an aerospace and defence power business and, with the AI datacentre power cycle, took the stock up about 200 percent in the year to August 2026.
